correctness.rationale: For each q>=2 and hub mass h>0, the centered maximal operator takes at the hub max(a,mu), and at a leaf max(b_i,(h a+b_i)/(h+1),mu). Coordinate maxima over positive linear averages commute with the weighted sum-of-squares maximum, and each nonnegative selector achieves its Hilbert norm on a nonnegative vector. Within-group permutation averaging of a nonnegative top generalized eigenvector gives the exact <=4 dimensional B_{r,k}; finite selector enumeration yields the 2*binom(q+2,2) formula. At h->0 the hub coordinate decouples and the remaining complete-graph selector has larger singular-value root Phi(k/q). At h->infty only selector G/all-I leaves has nonzero maximal first-order coefficient sqrt(q) h^-1/2, proving eventual dominance for fixed q; the two-level matrix gives Phi(q/(h+q)). I independently built all 18 full weighted selector matrices for q=2 and obtained winning patterns ING (and IGN) at h=1/10 with top squared norm 1.448834067224, INN at h=1 with 1.593070330817 and GII at h=100 with 1.129190655674, with exactly the specified rational characteristic factors. The package verify_weighted_star_maximal.py was read, not blindly trusted. The three examples prove >=2 phase changes, not a complete change count; numerical tests are not used as asymptotic proof.
